questions.question: Q1. What is the standard nominal bus speed for High-Speed CAN networks in modern electric vehicles?

explanations.b: Correct. High-Speed CAN operates at 500 kbps up to 1 Mbps.
explanations.c: 10 Gbps is high-performance fiber optic speed.

questions.question: Q2. Which field in a standard CAN frame determines arbitration priority on the bus?

explanations.a: Data payload contains the message content.
explanations.b: Correct. Lower numerical CAN ID values win arbitration over higher numerical IDs.
explanations.c: CRC is used for error detection.

questions.question: Q3. What consequence occurs when a Man-in-the-Middle (MiTM) attack intercepts and modifies throttle position sensor frames?

answers.a: The motor inverter receives false torque commands, causing unexpected acceleration or deceleration
answers.b: The battery pack instantly cools down to sub-zero temperatures
answers.d: The CAN bus physically converts from electrical to optical signaling

explanations.a: Correct. Altering throttle frames misleads the motor controller regarding actual driver intent.
explanations.b: MiTM attacks alter digital frames, not thermal cooling physics directly.
explanations.c: Headlights are managed on secondary LIN/CAN body nodes.

questions.question: Q4. How does an anomaly-based Intrusion Detection System identify un-cataloged zero-day attacks?

answers.a: By comparing live traffic behavior against statistical baseline models of normal communication
answers.b: By checking hardcoded virus signature lists from 10 years ago
answers.c: By shutting down the vehicle engine every 5 minutes
answers.d: By requiring biometric thumbprint scans from the driver

explanations.a: Correct. Anomaly detection monitors deviation in message frequency, timing, and sequence from learned normal baselines.
explanations.b: Static signatures cannot catch zero-day unknown attack patterns.
explanations.d: Biometrics authenticate human drivers, not internal ECU bus frames.

questions.question: Q5. What safety action should a Secure Vehicle Control Unit take upon detecting persistent spoofing attacks on critical motor control frames?

answers.a: Ignore the errors and continue running
answers.b: Transition to a restricted safe-state fail-soft mode and alert the driver
answers.c: Increase motor speed to maximum limit
answers.d: Clear all memory fault logs permanently

explanations.a: Ignoring attacks compromises vehicle occupant safety.
explanations.b: Correct. ISO 26262 functional safety mandates transitioning to a safe state (e.g. limp-home mode or controlled stop).
explanations.c: Increasing speed under attack increases hazard severity.
explanations.d: Clearing logs destroys diagnostic forensic evidence.

questions.question: Q6. What protocol extension adds payload encryption and authentication fields to automotive networks?

explanations.a: Correct. AUTOSAR SecOC adds Message Authentication Codes (MAC) and freshness values to CAN frames.
explanations.c: FTP is a file transfer protocol.
explanations.d: Telnet is an unencrypted legacy remote terminal protocol.

questions.question: Q7. What term describes an attack where an adversary records legitimate CAN traffic and re-transmits it later to execute unauthorized actions?

explanations.a: Correct. Replay attacks resend previously valid authenticated messages without needing secret key knowledge.
explanations.b: Buffer overflow is a memory corruption flaw.

questions.question: Q8. How does fresh counter verification prevent Replay Attacks in automotive networks?

answers.a: By ensuring each transmitted message includes a unique incrementing sequence counter
answers.b: By changing the CAN bus physical wire color
answers.d: By disconnecting the OBD-II diagnostic port

explanations.a: Correct. Receiver nodes reject messages containing stale or repeated sequence counters.
explanations.b: Wire color has no effect on cryptographic verification.
explanations.c: Current output is electrical power, not cryptographic counter.
explanations.d: OBD-II port is diagnostic access interface.

questions.question: Q9. What physical layer hardware feature makes CAN bus resistant to external electromagnetic interference (EMI)?

answers.b: Balanced differential signaling over twisted pair wires (CAN_H and CAN_L)

explanations.a: Unshielded single strand wire is highly susceptible to noise.
explanations.b: Correct. Differential voltage ($V_{\text{diff}} = V_{\text{CAN\_H}} - V_{\text{CAN\_L}}$) cancels out common-mode EMI noise.
explanations.c: High voltage AC lines induce interference rather than resisting it.
explanations.d: Infrared requires line-of-sight inside closed harnesses.

questions.question: Q10. What is the primary role of an OBD-II dongle firewall in protecting an EV's internal networks?

answers.a: To filter external diagnostic requests and prevent unauthorized access to internal powertrain CAN buses
answers.b: To replace the EV battery charger

explanations.a: Correct. OBD-II firewalls isolate the external diagnostic interface from critical powertrain control networks.
explanations.b: EV chargers are high-power AC/DC converters.
explanations.d: Coolant temperature is managed by thermal pumps.
